meta.title: How the market area changes a tax credit capture rate: a small-town Colorado example
meta.method: The example is a real small town in rural Colorado, within a half-hour drive of a regional city; its name, county and tracts are withheld. The project is the site tool's generic test: 60 family homes, 6 at 30% AMI, 12 at 50% and 42 at 60%. Qualified renter households come from the Housing-Analytics capture engine (js/market-analysis-scoring.js, chfaQualifiedRenters) on HUD CHAS 2018-2022 scaled to ACS 2020-2024 renters, under CHFA 2027-2028 rules (40% rent-to-income, occupancy limits by bedroom). Existing comparable homes are family tax credit homes at 60% AMI or below from the HUD LIHTC database, counted at the AMI levels the project serves. Drive times: 2020 Census blocks routed on the road network (OSRM, free-flow) from the town centre on 17 November 2026. Part-tract designs split each tract by the share of its 2020 population inside (blocks) or by each block group's low-income renters (ACS 2020-2024 B25003 and B19001). Commuter sheds: LODES 2024 tract-to-tract flows. Rental vacancy: ACS 2020-2024 B25004 and B25003. Land is rounded to the nearest 100 square miles and counts to the nearest 10; rates use unrounded counts.
meta.renter_owner: Every count is of RENTER households. Owners are not part of tax credit demand.
meta.capture_formula: CHFA capture = (project homes + existing comparable tax credit homes in the area) / income-qualified renter households (+ documented in-migration, if any). Net of occupied = project homes at 98% occupancy / (qualified - existing comparable homes at 98% occupancy); not a CHFA measure.
known_gaps: The site is withheld, so readers cannot rerun the example; the method can be rerun on any site in Market check.
CHAS is 2018-2022 and ACS 2020-2024; tract and block-group margins of error are wide, especially for rental vacancy and moves.
Block groups have no published income by tenure; the low-income renter share uses all households' incomes.
Drive times are free-flow from the town centre and do not reflect winter roads or traffic.
The HUD LIHTC database does not flag project-based Section 8 homes, which CHFA leaves out; city-area rates may be overstated.
Nothing here is a market study; CHFA requires one prepared by an approved analyst who discusses the market area with CHFA first.

rules.rule: Capture above 85% is not accepted without more data supporting demand.

rules.rule: CHFA favors a market area with low vacancy and few concessions; the study reports comparable vacancy by unit type with two years of history.

source.title: 2027-2028 Qualified Allocation Plan
source.quote: CHFA will look more favorably on a project that is in a PMA where there are lower vacancy rates and fewer concessions or reduced rents.
